critical_code_review_comments: server.py L353-359: CORS is configured with allow_credentials=False. This works today because the app is same-origin (frontend and API share https://shine-solutions-demo.preview.emergentagent.com), so the browser sends the cookie without needing CORS credentials. If in the future the frontend is served from a different origin, cookies WILL be blocked - set allow_credentials=True and pin allow_origins to explicit HTTPS origins (not '*').

server.py L279-280: response.set_cookie uses samesite='none' + secure=True which is correct for cross-site future-proofing, but forces HTTPS-only. Local http://localhost testing will not receive the cookie; document this in README/test_credentials.md (already implicitly enforced by REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL being HTTPS).

Admin.jsx L326-328: initial GET /api/auth/me on mount always fires even for unauthenticated visitors, generating a 401 console error on every /admin visit. Cosmetic only, but consider swallowing 401 without console noise (axios interceptor or catch that maps only) - the UX is fine.

server.py: /auth/logout does not require an authenticated session. Anyone can POST /api/auth/logout and it will just clear whatever cookie the caller has. Not a security issue (idempotent, no state change on server), but returning 200 without checking is a minor API-hygiene note.

Login response type LoginResponse now only exposes {email}; server.py L281 correctly no longer returns a token. Consider also stripping Set-Cookie visibility in logs if not already, since JWT is bearer-equivalent if leaked.

cookies are configured with a 12h max_age but the JWT `exp` is also 12h (create_access_token). They tick from slightly different origin times; if server clock drifts, cookie could outlive JWT (harmless - server rejects) or vice versa. Consider deriving cookie max_age from JWT exp to stay in sync.
